text: Two agents want to trade. Each has a private reserve price. Today's agent commerce makes them reveal it or trust a middleman who sees both. We seal both numbers in a Chainlink CRE Confidential Workflow instead.
The reserves are CRE Vault secrets, read once inside an AWS Nitro enclave via cre.handlerInTee. The overlap maths and the salted commitments never leave it.

The security property is the test suite: 34 workflow tests and 13 contract tests, with deliberately leaky implementations kept as negative controls. If a leaky seal ever passes, the checkers are broken.

The whole protocol for real: each agent vets the other (BlindOracle, x402 on Base), the enclave runs, and on SETTLE the DON writes the clearing price and commitments to a receiver on Base Sepolia. Then Agent A pays Agent B.
The receiver holds exactly three things per run: the clearing price (the midpoint), and two salted commitments. Neither reserve appears anywhere: not in a log, a report field, or a transaction.
Now the other case: the seller wants more than the buyer will pay.
NO_OVERLAP carries nothing: not the gap, not which side was higher. No transaction is sent, and the receiver contract itself reverts anything that is not a SETTLE.

Every payment is a USDC transfer you can check on Basescan; every settlement is a contract read. The one honest caveat: SETTLE reveals the sum of the two reserves. That is the standard sealed-bid trade-off, stated in the README.
Sealed-Bid Agent Settlement. Chainlink CRE, Base, BlindOracle. ETHOnline 2026.
